# EnterpriseGlue v0.35.2 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.35.1`.

## Highlights

- **runtime-dependencies:** Upgrade qs to 6.16.1 across the production dependency closure to repair CVE-2026-110816 query serialization denial of service.
- **frontend-host:** Keep substantial access-control editors within their existing settings navigation.

## User and administrator impact

- Runtime images use a patched query-string serialization dependency.
- Policy, custom-role, custom-permission, engine-set and project-target editors retain the Access Control page and section navigation.
- Alternate policy and Role Library entry points use the same bounded editor layout with unsaved-change protection.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrade to the qualified release images. Standalone consumers must refresh their own qs dependency resolution to 6.16.1 or later in the supported 6.x line.

## Database migrations

- The frozen bootstrap retains its existing predecessor code, migration inventory and schema-plan identity while refreshing its production dependency store.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- The workspace qs minimum is 6.16.1. Existing all-severity scanner gates and ignore policy remain unchanged.
- Preserve existing authorization, configuration ownership and broad-impact acknowledgements while protecting unsaved administrative changes.

- docs/runbooks/security-dependency-updates.md
- docs/development/identity-access-ui-evidence-report.md

## Known limitations

- Exact-image security, supported database adapters and real-engine browser qualification remain required before publication.

## Rollback

- Prefer a qualified forward release. Restoring qs 6.16.0 restores the known denial-of-service risk.
- Restore the previous frontend-host package; no data migration is required.

## Validation evidence

- Twenty-two focused dependency and frozen-bootstrap contracts pass, including eight malformed comma-serialization combinations and ordinary query behavior.
- Published-package version planning and release-note preflight pass. Exact-image security, all supported database adapters and the real-engine browser candidate gates remain required before publication.
- Platform-administration unit gate: 35 files and 176 tests passed.
- 27 workflow cases passed across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including compact group-dialog and unchanged role-scope regression checks.
- 23 existing Access Control resource-grant, layout/accessibility and identity-administration browser cases passed in Chromium.
- Frontend-host compilation, frontend TypeScript check, production build and bundle budget passed; seven UI screenshots were refreshed and audited.
- Browser checks use deterministic API fixtures. The frontend-only change has no backend, schema or database migration changes.
